A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-ZVP research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results for Qwen3 models, comparisons with GRPO and filtering baselines, component and scaling-factor ablations, and NuminaMath experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds out-of-domain evaluation, further ablations, and training-dynamics analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed RL-ZVP procedure, entropy-guided advantage, objective, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The symmetric variant introduced in Appendix C.2 is an experimental control, rather than a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix B.2 adds evaluation beyond mathematics: LiveCodeBench coding, MMLU-Pro knowledge, GPQA-Diamond scientific reasoning, and BIG-Bench Hard logical reasoning. This substantially broadens task coverage. The NuminaMath training experiments already appeared in v1 Appendix A.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 introduces the untrained base model as a comparator, and Table 9 adds a symmetric RL-ZVP variant. Figure 7 also adds GRPO-DS and GRESO to the training-dynamics comparison previously showing only GRPO and RL-ZVP. The main benchmark comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: Added experiments use selected MMLU-Pro subjects and BIG-Bench Hard subsets, a symmetric-penalty control, and additional alpha settings of 0.001, 0.01, 1, and 10. Existing training budgets, checkpoint-selection procedures, sampling settings, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Explicitly listing the main alpha setting is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 Appendices C–E substantially extend the analyses: a wider alpha sensitivity sweep, a direct test of asymmetric versus symmetric penalties, filtering-baseline training trajectories, and comparison of zero-variance prevalence on NuminaMath and DAPO-Math-17k. The original component ablations and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The earlier numerical result tables are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial outcomes in Tables 7–9 and Figures 7–8. For example, Table 7 reports out-of-domain average Acc@8/Pass@8 of 30.19/55.36 for RL-ZVP versus 27.84/52.84 for GRPO. Table 9 newly reports 46.64/66.15 for the symmetric variant versus 49.90/69.77 for RL-ZVP.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 8 adds a mathematical definition of the symmetric control, assigning positive advantage alpha times entropy and negative advantage its exact opposite. Equations 1–7, the gradient derivation, and the existing formal remarks are unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about extracting learning signals from zero-variance prompts, generalizing GRPO through entropy-guided advantages, improving reasoning and training stability, and outperforming filtering baselines. The headline performance and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning cross-domain transfer, the benefit of asymmetric penalties, and possible entropy explosion in filtering baselines. It removes the concluding limitation about fixed-alpha sensitivity and adaptive scheduling, although sensitivity remains discussed elsewhere. The new claim of outperforming all out-of-domain baselines overstates Table 7, which contains BIG-Bench Hard exceptions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and explicitly lists alpha = 0.10 for both main training configurations in Table 5. The hardware, framework, remaining hyperparameters, and checkpoint-selection details match v1 Appendix C, relocated to v2 Appendix A. The PDFs establish the added link, without establishing what resources it provides.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a fine-grained reward-shaping paragraph explaining how RL-ZVP addresses advantage vanishing left unresolved by token-level shaping methods. Four benchmark references accompany the new out-of-domain evaluations. The broader positioning against GRPO and prompt filtering is retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introduction's motivation, adds a related-work paragraph, reorganizes the appendices, and adds correspondence information and an LLM-use disclosure. Most existing method, results, and qualitative-example text remains unchanged, so the revision is not an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables covering transfer and further ablations, plus two figures covering additional training dynamics and zero-variance prevalence. It moves v1 Table 5 and Figure 6 from the appendix into the main text as Table 1 and Figure 4. These changes substantially expand and reorganize the visual evidence; existing figures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The out-of-domain tests and symmetric-penalty ablation strengthen evidence for transfer and the specific advantage design, while the wider alpha sweep and explicit default improve characterization and reproducibility. These extend an already substantial empirical study. Benefits are tempered by unchanged uncertainty reporting, an overbroad superiority statement contradicted by Table 7's BIG-Bench Hard results, and removal of the concluding alpha-sensitivity caveat. The net improvement is supported but limited.
